stem:
Om notices that one festival linked only to Moon phases falls on different Gregorian dates in different years. Another festival tied to the solar year falls on nearly the same Gregorian date each year. A third system mixes Moon months with solar-year corrections.

Which claim correctly matches festival-date behaviour to the calendar system?

options.text: A purely lunar festival shifts across Gregorian dates from year to year, while a solar festival stays near the same Gregorian date.
A purely lunar festival always falls on the same Gregorian date every year.
A solar festival must shift by about a month each year on the Gregorian calendar.
Luni-solar systems ignore the Moon and use only the solar year.

teacher.key_rationale: Purely lunar dates drift on the Gregorian calendar; solar festivals stay near a fixed Gregorian date. Luni-solar systems keep Moon months but correct to the solar year.
